![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14210206/assets/8b4196d82bf27236e6c28651a01678c60c41bc851afbb7aad2e754578ba330e9.png)

Jacob is a carpenter. He wishes to reduce the size of a wooden square while maintaining its shape. The lengths of the diagonals of the square decrease at a rate of $2\text{ cm}\text{/h}.$ At what rate, in squared centimeters per hour, is the area of ​​the square decreasing when the length of the diagonal is $45\,\text{cm}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let $h$ and $A$ be the length of the diagonals and the area of the square, respectively. Using the Pythagorean theorem, it can be shown that the relationship between $A$ and $h$ is

$$
A=\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}.
$$

We want to find

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}.
$$

Differentiating this relationship with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(A) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}h}(\frac{{h}^{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\cdot h.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $h$ decreases at a rate of $2\,\text{cm/h},$ so

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we want to compute the rate of change of the area when the diagonal has length $h=45.$ Substituting this information into our expression for $\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t} & =-2\cdot 45=-90\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\text{/h}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that the area of the square is decreasing at a rate of $90\,{\text{cm}}^{2}\text{/h}.$
